market_context: U.S. equities are staging an explosive relief rally Monday following Nvidia's surprise reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO and CrowdStrike's $44B acquisition of Zscaler, partially rebounding from last week's severe tech sell-off. However, with the 10-year Treasury yield still elevated near 4.95% and ongoing SEC scrutiny surrounding Nvidia's accounting, the initial opening gap-and-go euphoria is facing intraday resistance and profit-taking across mega-cap tech.

predictions.reasoning: After gapping up over 4.6% to test resistance near $724.81, the S&P 500 is extended relative to technical moving averages following seven consecutive losing sessions. With the 10-year Treasury yield sticky at 4.95% and macro caution ahead of the upcoming PCE report, morning relief gains are likely to see afternoon consolidation toward the middle of the day's range.

QQQ surged nearly 7% at the open but has already met selling pressure after touching an intraday high of $656.25. As short-covering flows subside following the initial headline pop, high-valuation growth names face headwinds from stubborn long-term bond yields, driving a modest intraday fade into the close.

NVDA's massive +34.7% surge upon Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO has pushed shares directly into overhead resistance around $165-$170, just off session highs of $169.29. While leadership clarity removes immediate governance panic, the reported SEC accounting inquiry remains an unresolved overhang, prompting institutional profit-taking off peak morning levels.

Tesla joined the broader tech beta squeeze, jumping over 12% to test morning highs of $389.59. High-beta momentum stocks typically give back a portion of outsized opening surges once broad market liquidity normalizes in the afternoon session.
